title: Kong Empire founded
description: Dyula traders and warriors build a state at Kong that commands the trade between the forest and the Niger.

title: French colony established
description: France formally organises Côte d'Ivoire as a colony under its first governor, Louis-Gustave Binger, and pushes inland with treaties and troops.

title: Capital moved to Bingerville
description: Yellow fever drives the colonial administration from the insalubrious coast at Grand-Bassam up the lagune to Bingerville.

title: Abidjan becomes capital
description: The seat of government moves to the rising terminus of the railway on the Ebrié lagoon.

title: African planters' union founded
description: Félix Houphouët-Boigny, a cocoa planter and chief, founds the Syndicat Agricole Africain, the seed of the movement that will govern the country for fifty years.

title: Vridi Canal opens
description: A channel through the sand bar gives Abidjan a deep-water port and launches the export boom later called the Ivorian miracle.

title: Republic proclaimed
description: After voting to stay in the French Community, Côte d'Ivoire becomes a self-governing republic with Houphouët-Boigny at its head.

title: Independence from France
description: Côte d'Ivoire becomes fully independent under President Félix Houphouët-Boigny.

title: Houphouët-Boigny elected president
description: The national assembly elects Houphouët-Boigny president, beginning thirty-three years of unbroken PDCI rule.

title: Capital moved to Yamoussoukro
description: The assembly designates the president's home village the political capital, though government business largely stays in Abidjan.

title: First multiparty presidential election
description: After months of strikes, Houphouët-Boigny legalises opposition and defeats Laurent Gbagbo.

title: Death of Houphouët-Boigny
description: The father of the nation dies in office, and Henri Konan Bédié succeeds him as the constitution provides.

title: First coup
description: Mutinous soldiers overthrow Bédié and install General Robert Guéï, ending nearly forty years of civilian politics.

title: Gbagbo installed by street pressure
description: Guéï claims victory and is driven out by street protests; Laurent Gbagbo is sworn in while northern candidates are barred from the ballot.

title: Civil war divides the country
description: A failed coup becomes a rebel seizure of the north; French and UN forces police a frozen north-south partition for five years.

title: Bouaké airstrike and anti-French riots
description: Government jets hit a French base while bombing rebels; France destroys the Ivorian air force and mobs attack French residents in Abidjan.

title: Toxic waste scandal
description: Residues dumped by a Dutch-registered tanker sicken tens of thousands and bring down the transitional government.

title: Ouagadougou peace agreement
description: Gbagbo and rebel leader Guillaume Soro agree on a unity government and elections, ending the partition.

title: Standoff after the 2010 election
description: Gbagbo refuses to concede defeat to Alassane Ouattara, and the country has two presidents until force decides the matter.

title: Gbagbo arrested
description: After weeks of fighting and UN and French bombardment, Ouattara's forces take Gbagbo from his bunker, ending the second civil war.

title: Ouattara re-elected
description: Alassane Ouattara wins a second term with more than four-fifths of the vote in an election held in general calm.

title: Grand-Bassam attack
description: Al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb gunmen open fire on the beach hotels of the old colonial town, killing nineteen people.
